videos.title: How to use BOTH Refined Storage and Storage Drawers - Tutorial (Minecraft 1.16.5)

order.note: A plain wooden drawer first - 1x1 for bulk, 2x1 or 2x2 when you want more item types per block. Guides pick the 2x2 as the default workhorse.

The upgrade template is the second craft and the thing that unlocks the mod's whole upgrade column. It is made from a drawer plus a wooden rod, so the first drawer is literally consumed to open the tree.
A drawer key early - it is what lets you lock a drawer to an item so an empty drawer keeps its assignment.
The controller is the late structural piece, not an early one: it needs a comparator, a diamond, stone and a drawer.

ladder.note: CAPACITY LADDER, VERIFIED FROM THE JAR'S OWN LANG FILE - the roman numerals are authoritative and material order is NOT the tier order. Obsidian is tier I (the cheapest, earliest rung) and emerald sits above gold. Ranking these by material value would put the first rung last.

Structural ladder: loose drawers -> a controller that presents the whole bank as one inventory -> slaves to extend its reach -> remote upgrades so a drawer group can join a controller without touching it.
Magnet upgrade has its own three-rung tier line, separate from capacity.

gates.note: Every single storage upgrade AND the drawer key are gated on the upgrade template, which is itself gated on already owning a drawer. Nothing in the upgrade column is reachable before a drawer exists.
The controller needs a comparator and a diamond, so the mod's payoff moment sits behind nether quartz and diamonds - later than its cheap wooden drawers suggest.
Compacting drawers convert between ingot/block forms and only accept items that have such a recipe - they are not general-purpose drawers.

payoff.note: The controller is unambiguously the moment the mod clicks: a wall of drawers stops being furniture and becomes one searchable inventory you can pull from and push to.
Quantify and fill-level readouts are the quiet win - you can read stock levels off the wall without opening anything.
Void upgrade plus a locked drawer is the classic cobblestone answer - overflow is destroyed instead of clogging the system.

traps.note: Two upgrades are config-disabled by default and the jar ships explicit 'Has no effect with current mod configuration' warning strings for them. Verify the pack config before making either a quest target.
The one-stack upgrade is a DOWNGRADE despite the name - the lang string calls it 'Storage Downgrade' and it cuts a drawer to a single stack. Do not place it on a progression ladder.
Creative upgrades are creative-only and must never appear as quest tasks or rewards.

signature.note: The drawer itself plus the controller - the mod is those two ideas and everything else is a modifier.
The key family is what makes drawers behave like a managed system rather than shelves.
